rationale: Billed line: CPT 17110 - Destruction of benign lesion(s). Review of the medical record shows direct, consistent documentation that the planned and performed procedure was destruction of a single benign seborrheic keratosis on the mid-back under local anesthesia. Operative documentation: Operative Note documents the procedure as performed and names CPT 17110 (Operative Note, NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_08.pdf-n25, p.25) [ev1]; the operative technique documents a single 0.8 cm lesion at T7 and that the lesion was destroyed using sharp curettage with light electrodesiccation (Operative Note, NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_08.pdf-n25, p.25) [ev2, ev3]. Brief Postoperative Note repeats the performed procedure and CPT 17110 (Brief Postoperative Note, NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_08.pdf-n27, p.27) [ev4]. Pre-operative assessment lists the planned procedure as CPT 17110 (Pre-Operative Assessment & Anesthesia Evaluation, NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_08.pdf-n16, p.16) [ev5]. Informed consent documents consent for removal of the benign seborrheic keratosis, mid-back (Informed Consent Documentation, NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_08.pdf-n10, p.11) [ev6]. The operative note further documents no additional lesions treated and that no specimen was submitted (Operative Summary, NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_08.pdf-n25, p.26) [ev3]. The governing APC policy query returned no target policy concept specific to CPT 17110; the APC concept returned pertains to same-day E/M modifier -25 (non-target for 17110) and therefore does not impose an additional technique/size/extent requirement that would contradict the documentation for this procedure (RULE-Policy-Documents-APC-APC_Policy_Concepts.xlsx-APC-08-9-code; APC concept note) [ev7]. Conclusion: the clinical record documents the lesion, the method of destruction, single-lesion extent, local anesthesia, and informed consent consistent with CPT 17110. Therefore the billed line is supported as submitted. NOTE: the claim also contains a same-day E/M (99213-25); the retrieved APC policy text about modifier -25 is non-target to 17110. This review addressed only line 1 (17110); no change to line 1 is indicated. Billed line: CPT 99213-25 (office/outpatient established patient visit, low-to-moderate complexity with modifier -25) on same day as CPT 17110. Governing policy (APC-08) requires that modifier -25 be supported by documentation of a significant, separately identifiable E/M service beyond the routine pre-/post-procedure work, including a dedicated history/exam and a distinct assessment and plan for the additional complaint (e.g., diagnostic workup ordered, referral made, or treatment initiated) (RULE-Policy-Documents-APC-APC_Policy_Concepts.xlsx-APC-08-4, section: APC Coding Concept - Modifier -25 on Same-Day E/M with a Minor Procedure). The medical record does not meet those requirements: - The History & Physical documents the chest symptom only in the review-of-systems: Cardiovascular: Patient mentions occasional intermittent chest discomfort over the past month, non-exertional, resolves spontaneously; denies palpitations, diaphoresis, or radiation (NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_08.pdf-n4, p.4). This is the kind of ROS-only documentation the policy says is insufficient to support -25. - The Post-Procedure/Progress Note documents that the chest complaint was not worked up during this encounter and that no EKG, labs, or cardiology referral were ordered (NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_08.pdf-n37, p.38). Specifically: Chest discomfort mentioned during review of systems was noted but not further worked up today; no EKG, labs, or cardiology referral ordered (NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_08.pdf-n37, p.38). - The Operative Note explicitly states there was no separate evaluation beyond routine pre-procedure review performed or documented during the encounter: No separate cardiac evaluation, telemetry, or additional history-taking beyond the routine pre-procedure review was performed or documented during this encounter (NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_08.pdf-n25, p.25). Taken together, the record documents only a ROS-level mention of chest discomfort without an expanded history/exam or any distinct assessment/plan tied to that complaint, and the operative/post-op notes explicitly state no separate evaluation or workup occurred. Under the governing policy (Modifier -25 requires a significant, separately identifiable E/M service; Supporting documentation should include a dedicated history and exam ... and, critically, a distinct assessment and plan), the documentation does not support billing 99213-25 on the same day as the minor procedure. Correction: remove CPT 99213-25 (no replacement code); modifier -25 is not supported by the chart. Evidence: RULE-Policy-Documents-APC-APC_Policy_Concepts.xlsx-APC-08-4 (policy), NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_08.pdf-n4 p.4 (H&P), NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_08.pdf-n37 p.38 (Post-Procedure Note), NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_08.pdf-n25 p.25 (Operative Note).

evidence.quote: PROCEDURE PERFORMED: Destruction of benign skin lesion, mid-back (CPT 17110)

The target lesion was identified as a 0.8 cm raised, verrucous, hyperpigmented lesion consistent with the previously biopsied benign seborrheic keratosis, located just lateral to the T7 spinous process.
the lesion was destroyed using a combination of sharp curettage and light electrodesiccation with the hyfrecator to achieve hemostasis at the base.
Procedure Performed: Destruction of benign skin lesion, mid-back (CPT 17110)
Planned Procedure: Destruction of benign skin lesion, mid-back (CPT 17110)
of the following procedure: Benign seborrheic keratosis, mid-back.
No separate cardiac evaluation, telemetry, or additional history-taking beyond the routine pre-procedure review was performed or documented during this encounter.
Chest discomfort mentioned during review of systems was noted but not further worked up today; no EKG, labs, or cardiology referral ordered
Cardiovascular: Patient mentions occasional intermittent chest discomfort over the past month, non-exertional, resolves spontaneously; denies palpitations, diaphoresis, or radiation.

policy_citations.quote: Modifier -25 requires a significant, separately identifiable E/M service above and beyond the usual pre- and post-procedure work already bundled into a scheduled minor procedure.

Supporting documentation should include a dedicated history and exam addressing the additional complaint and, critically, a distinct assessment and plan (e.g., diagnostic workup ordered, referral made, or treatment initiated) for that complaint.

rationale_letter: Re: Claim APC-2026-30442 / Patient MRN-2245173 Dear Provider, We performed an audit of line 2 on the above claim, CPT 99213-25 (office/outpatient visit, established patient, low-to-moderate complexity with modifier -25), billed same-day as CPT 17110 (destruction of benign lesion). The governing APC policy for same-day E/M with a minor procedure (APC-08) requires documentation of a significant, separately identifiable E/M service in addition to routine pre- and post-procedure work. Specifically, supporting documentation must include a dedicated history and exam addressing the additional complaint and a distinct assessment and plan (for example, ordering diagnostic testing, initiating treatment, or making a referral). Basis for Finding: - The History & Physical documents only a review-of-systems mention of chest discomfort: Cardiovascular: Patient mentions occasional intermittent chest discomfort over the past month, non-exertional, resolves spontaneously; denies palpitations, diaphoresis, or radiation (History & Physical, NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_08.pdf-n4, p.4). The APC policy explicitly states that a complaint that appears only within a review-of-systems checklist without an expanded history, targeted exam, or resulting plan does not meet the threshold for modifier -25 (RULE-Policy-Documents-APC-APC_Policy_Concepts.xlsx-APC-08-4). - The Post-Procedure Progress Note documents that the chest complaint was noted but not worked up during this encounter and that no EKG, labs, or cardiology referral were ordered (Physician Progress / Post-Procedure Note, NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_08.pdf-n37, p.38). This demonstrates no distinct assessment or plan addressing the chest complaint on the same day. - The Operative Note explicitly states that no separate evaluation beyond the routine pre-procedure review was performed or documented for this encounter: No separate cardiac evaluation, telemetry, or additional history-taking beyond the routine pre-procedure review was performed or documented during this encounter (Operative Note, NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_08.pdf-n25, p.25). Determination and Correction: Because the chart lacks documentation of a separately identifiable E/M service (expanded HPI/exam and a distinct assessment/plan) on the same day as the minor procedure, the modifier -25 is not supported and CPT 99213-25 should be removed. No replacement procedure code is appropriate for this documented encounter. If you disagree with this determination, please provide contemporaneous documentation demonstrating a separately identifiable E/M service on the same date (for example, a focused history and exam addressing the chest complaint plus a distinct assessment and specific orders or referrals generated on that date) for reconsideration. Sincerely, Clinical Claims Audit Team
